candidate.negationProofTerm:
by
  intro h
  have hdist :
      ((0, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) ≠ ((1, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) ∧
      ((0, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) ≠ ((2, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) ∧
      ((0, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) ≠ ((3, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) ∧
      ((1, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) ≠ ((2, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) ∧
      ((1, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) ≠ ((3, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) ∧
      ((2, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) ≠ ((3, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) := by
    repeat' constructor
    all_goals
      intro hEq
      have hfirst := (Prod.ext_iff.mp hEq).1
      norm_num at hfirst
  have hiff := h ((0, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) ((1, 0) : ℝ × ℝ)
      ((2, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) ((3, 0) : ℝ × ℝ) hdist
  have hdet : Matrix.det
      !![(0 : ℝ) ^ 2 + (0 : ℝ) ^ 2, (0 : ℝ), (0 : ℝ), (1 : ℝ);
         (1 : ℝ) ^ 2 + (0 : ℝ) ^ 2, (1 : ℝ), (0 : ℝ), (1 : ℝ);
         (2 : ℝ) ^ 2 + (0 : ℝ) ^ 2, (2 : ℝ), (0 : ℝ), (1 : ℝ);
         (3 : ℝ) ^ 2 + (0 : ℝ) ^ 2, (3 : ℝ), (0 : ℝ), (1 : ℝ)] = 0 := by
    exact Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_column_eq_zero (i := (2 : Fin 4)) (by
      intro j
      fin_cases j <;> simp)
  have hcon := hiff.mpr hdet
  rcases hcon with ⟨cx, cy, r, hr, h1, h2, h3, h4⟩
  simp at h1 h2 h3 h4
  nlinarith [h1, h2, h3]
candidate.counterexampleDescription: Take the four distinct collinear points (0,0), (1,0), (2,0), (3,0). The determinant matrix has third column identically zero, so the determinant is 0. But no circle with positive radius can pass through four distinct points on the same line, since a line meets a circle in at most two points. Thus the claimed iff fails.
